text: Northern Ireland's Rory McIlroy on day three of the Scottish Open 2025 at The Renaissance Club, North Berwick

McIlroy, who came in second at the Irish Open held at Royal County Down last year, acknowledges that he was unprepared for the overwhelming support he experienced at Portrush in 2019, as he attempted to distance himself from the excitement surrounding his inaugural major event on home soil.

Rory McIlroy from Holywood is considered one of the favorites for The Open, while Shane Lowry from Ireland aims to secure a victory in Portrush, similar to his triumph in 2019 when the championship last took place in the coastal town.

On Monday morning, the world number two, who claimed his Open title at Hoylake in 2014, thrilled the large crowds by sinking a birdie putt on the 18th green and then spent 15 minutes signing autographs.

Although the world number two did not make the cut at the same venue in 2019, he has steadily accumulated victories over the years, with the most significant being his completion of the career Grand Slam by winning the Masters in April.
